h: Chippendale, a Princess and a Himalayan Garden
p: Harewood has a special link with Thomas Chippendale, the famous furniture maker, who was born just up the road in Otley. He made a large amount of furniture for the house, and seeing his work in the rooms it was designed for is a real treat for anyone who loves craftsmanship. Royal watchers will be interested to know that Princess Mary, daughter of King George V, lived here as Countess of Harewood and later Princess Royal, and the house has plenty of reminders of her time.

Outdoors, the Himalayan Garden is a lovely surprise, with a stream tumbling through rhododendrons and other plants from the mountains, and a Buddhist stupa tucked into the planting. The walled garden and the terraces by the house are full of colour in summer, and the lakeside walk is a peaceful loop. Families should seek out the adventure playground, which gives kids a well-earned break from the grown-up stuff.
Allow a full day if you want house, gardens and play, as the estate is large. Comfortable shoes are a must for the hills, and bring a layer in case the wind picks up.

Cycling fans may remember that the 2014 Tour de France got under way from Harewood. Nearby, the spa town of Harrogate, with its Valley Gardens and famous tea rooms, is a short drive north, and the market town of Otley is great for a riverside stroll.
